CrewSkip.setting_step: Game seconds a time-skip moves at a time while a machine runs or a crew order is on, from 1 to 60. Each step takes about the same real time whatever its length, so a longer step means a shorter freeze. 30 is the default. What a long step costs: crew take their next job only when a step ends; a machine that finishes a batch partway through a step may wait for the next step to start another; each MHD generator is topped up once a step, so on its own it feeds about 240 kW at 30 seconds and 120 kW at 60 (batteries supply too); and a busy machine in a small room can wait for cooler air all skip. 1 is the most faithful and the slowest: it is how skips with crew orders ran before Framework 0.112.0, when a six-hour skip could freeze the game for minutes.
RoomHeat.setting: How much of their heat Phobos machines give off, from 0.05 to 1. 0.25, the default, means a quarter of the heat they gave before Framework 0.94.0; 1 restores it. It covers the heat machines put into their room and the mining laser's heat into a cooling assembly. Fires and explosions are not affected.

SharedLines.gas_description:
A plant earns its berth when the supplies can reach it. Fennmark gas line joins your stores and machines on one sealed run, laid under or beside the equipment it serves. Touching equipment joins directly; pipe gives you room to arrange the rest. It shares tiles with other kinds of line.

Each tile holds a few grams of gas once supplied and keeps them there. Vent the line before taking it up. The cheapest gas on your manifest is still worth keeping out of the cabin.
SharedLines.water_description:
Fennmark process-water line keeps the growing and working parts of your ship supplied without a parade of carried containers. A connected run under or beside tanks and machines joins them; touching equipment needs no extra pipe. Process grade only: it does not connect to drinking water.

The pipe holds about half a kilogram of water per tile once supplied and retains it. Drain into a canister before taking it up. Water has paid its freight to get aboard. Give it a proper route to its next job.
SharedLines.belt_description:
Rivetline puts the hauling route on the deck. These conveyor segments move loose items between compatible machines, collectors and stores, leaving the crew more time for the work a belt cannot do. Run the belt under or beside both ends; equipment within one tile needs no intervening belt. Pipe and line can share its tile in their own lanes.

The belt holds no cargo: items pass directly while the sending or receiving machine has power. Your products still need somewhere to land. A quicker route across the workroom is no substitute for an empty tray.

WaterTanks.description:
Rivetline's S-series silos keep a useful reserve between the dock and the next working shift. This {2} x {2} silo holds {1:F0} kg of process water in a {0:F0} kg housing. Fill from station Bulk supplies or a linked plant, such as a T2 thaw unit, and let several machines share the reserve.

Connections reach the port beside the middle of the left-hand side, by touching equipment or process-water line. With Ship's Water installed, drinking-water tanks can supply process work and the silo can return water to its waste tanks for the Recycler. The silo itself supplies no drinking water. Damage traps its contents in a catch chamber: repair, then recover them. The water you brought this far deserves another shift.

DrainCanister.name: Drain Canister
DrainCanister.description:
A sound line can still need taking up. Rivetline's D20 gives its liquid somewhere to go first: a {0:0} litre lined drain canister, {1:0} kg empty, ready for the next change to your ship's plumbing.

Use Drain line into canister, then haul the full can into a tank holding the same liquid. It pours in and leaves the empty can ready to use again. One liquid at a time. Recover the contents before you move the pipe, and the next installation starts with one fewer loss to replace.
